subject: Post-call: PayFlow budget path, token economics & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@payflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PayFlow budget path, token economics & next steps

Hi Alicia — great to chat earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align with your budget window. Thanks again for sharing upfront context.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- High latency for multi-turn receipts processing (SLA target: sub-250ms for critical routes).
- Token burn for real-time user summaries is the dominant cost; current infra spend is unpredictable month-to-month.
- Procurement needs a clear TCO path and commitment/fallback options so legal/finance can sign off.

Goals we heard:
- 40–50% reduction in inference-driven token spend within a 90–120 day pilot while keeping model quality at parity.
- A deterministic cost envelope for the product team to bring to leadership and procurement.
- Proof-of-concept showing latency improvement on 10k/day peak flows.

Cost levers we discussed (high level):
- Batching: group low-size requests from the receipts microservice to gain 30–60% token latency tradeoffs depending on spike profiles.
- KV/prefix caching: store common system prompts and recent conversation prefixes to avoid repeated context tokens; expect 15–35% token reduction for mid-length conversations.
- Model mix routing: steer non-critical work to a quantized variant during high load to keep SLA and control unit cost.
- Session-level rate shaping: cap peak qps for non-critical user flows with a burst allowance during payroll spikes.

Attached: payflow_tco_draft.xlsx — a first-pass cost model with three scenarios (baseline, batching+cache, full-commit). Numbers are illustrative; we'll refine with your traffic histogram.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) You share a 7-day token histogram (by route) — we’ll plug into the TCO model (by EOD Mon, Apr 2).
2) We run a short latency runbook on a staging snapshot (2–3 business days) and share expected tail latency improvements.
3) If economics line up, draft SOW and a 60-day pilot with defined success criteria (target: >=40% token reduction or SLA improvement).

Can you confirm: (a) who on your engineering side owns the traffic histogram, and (b) whether procurement wants line-item unit costs or a vendor-blended TCO figure?

Thanks — look forward to aligning calendars.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: payflow_tco_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 sheets)

From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@payflow.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Lars Engstrom <lars.engstrom@payflow.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayFlow budget path, token economics & next steps

Thanks Marcus — helpful recap and appreciated the clear next steps. Quick answers inline: 

- I’ll pull the 7-day histogram for receipts and the user-summary route; that’s owned by our infra team (Lars is looping in). Expect a dropbox link by Monday morning.
- Procurement will want a vendor-blended TCO figure for their initial deck; they may ask for line-items later during contracting.

Two asks from my side: 
1) Can you include a short appendix in the TCO workbook that shows sensitivity to sequence length distribution (we have bursts with long receipts during tax season).
2) Any quick wins we can do in-app (client-side truncation or pre-filtering) to reduce tokens before we touch batching? Our product team prefers small client-side changes if it reduces immediate spend.

I’ll get the histogram and a short ops note from Lars.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Moreno
Head of Product | PayFlow Inc
alicia@payflow.com

Attachment: payflow_internal_budget.pdf (internal budgeting memo)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@payflow.com>, Lars Engstrom <lars.engstrom@payflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayFlow budget path, token economics & next steps

Perfect — thanks Alicia. Quick responses: 

- I’ll add a sensitivity tab to the TCO workbook for sequence-length distribution and a short note on how we model tax-season long-tail events.
- Client-side micro-optimizations: yes — common approaches are prompt truncation, ephemeral summary caching on the client, and removing verbose system prompts for known flows. We’ll list those as "quick wins" in the appendix so your product team can triage.

Operational ask: Lars / engineering — could you paste the histogram link into this thread when available? We’ll treat that as the canonical input. Once we have it we’ll run the three-scenario model and follow up with a 45-minute economics review.

Also looping in Marissa (CS lead) on pilot ops and Karthik (solutions architect) for model-routing notes. Proposed window for pilot: mid-April start, 60 days. If you need a software-only proofing window first, we can compress to a 30-day test with narrower success criteria.

Next meeting suggestion: 45-minute TCO review Wed Apr 4 or Thu Apr 5 — which works for you?

— Marcus

Attachment: (updated) payflow_tco_draft.xlsx (will add sensitivity tab after histogram)

From: procurement@payflow.com <procurement@payflow.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayFlow budget path, token economics & next steps

Marcus — looping procurement questions in early. Two items we need clarified before pilot SOW: 

1) Security/compliance: confirm that Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report and data separation guarantees during a dedicated pilot (isolation on dedicated capacity).
2) Pricing cadence & overage: we need unit-price definitions (per-token or per-embed), expected monthly invoicing cadence, and a mechanism for capping spend during pilot phase.

Please reply with a short summary we can attach to our vendor comparison spreadsheet.

Thanks,
PayFlow Procurement (procurement@payflow.com)

Note: Lars is cc'd on their technical answers; Alicia remains the business owner for the deal.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: procurement@payflow.com, Alicia Moreno <alicia@payflow.com>, Lars Engstrom <lars.engstrom@payflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayFlow budget path, token economics & next steps

Thanks — answering procurement's two items below for your spreadsheet. Happy to provide these as a short PDF as well.

1) Security/compliance: Redwood can provide a SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; for pilots that require isolation we offer Redwood Dedicated which provisions a customer-dedicated GPU pool and network isolation. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS) and audit log exports for the pilot duration. Notes: SOC 2 report available upon request; Dedicated provisioning lead time ~2–3 weeks depending on cloud region.

2) Pricing cadence & overage: pilot pricing options we typically present:
   - Usage pilot (no commitment): per-token pricing with monthly invoicing; pilot cap can be enforced via rate limits + billing alerts.
   - Committed pilot (recommended for predictable budget): a short-term committed pool (60 days) with a blended per-token effective price plus overage band at a pre-agreed rate.
   - Billing cadence: monthly invoices with itemized token/embedding breakout; Procurement can choose an invoice cap and we’ll stop/notify on threshold breach.

For your vendor spreadsheet, suggested one-paragraph summary: "Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II (report provided under NDA), customer-dedicated pilot capacity for isolation, and flexible pilot pricing (usage or short-term commitment) with monthly invoices, itemized token metrics, and optional spend caps enforced via rate limits."

Next step: once we have the histogram, we’ll populate the TCO workbook and schedule the 45-minute review. I’ll export a two-page vendor summary for procurement to attach to your comparison.

— Marcus

Attachment: vendor_summary_redwood.pdf (short answers to procurement)
